rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmit through Sulaym b. Amir that Umar asked why some dreams prove true; Ali answered that all souls are taken, and visions seen while in heaven are true.
rows.anchor: فقال علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

words: فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In Ali's account, souls released to their bodies encounter devils in the air, who mix falsehood into what they saw, making those dreams false.
rows.anchor: إذا أرسلت إلى أجسادها تلقتها الشياطين في الهواء فكذبتها وأخبرتها بالأباطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's apparent picture of the sleeping soul held in heaven until release needs interpretation if the soul is immaterial; this is not required by the alternative view of the soul.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذا الأثر أن النفس النائمة المقبوضة تكون في السماء حتى ترسل ومثل ذلك مما يجب تأويله على القول بتجرد النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi describes the noble, celestial soul as descending to govern its bodily home, then using sleep as an opportunity to turn toward the world of light and receive some of its effects.
rows.anchor: إن النفس شريفة علوية هبطت من المحل الأرفع وأرسلت من حمة ممنع وشغلت بتدبير منزلها

words: فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul receiving from the perfected world of light sees true dreams; one turning back toward its worldly governance, amid delusions, sees false dreams, though individuals differ in readiness and insight.
rows.anchor: فمتى رأت وهي تلك الحال مستفيضة من ذلك العالم الموصوف بالكمال رؤيا كانت صادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the described taking, retaining, and releasing of souls; its distance-form reflects the starting point, the fact that it was just mentioned, or its exalted rank.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما ذكر من التوفي والإمساك والإرسال والإفراد لتأويله بالمذكور أو نحوه وصيغة البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nunation of signs conveys abundance and greatness: the account supplies many magnificent proofs of God's power, wisdom, and encompassing mercy.
rows.anchor: للتكثير والتعظيم أي إن فيما ذكر الآيات كثيرة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflectors consider how souls attach to bodies and are wholly taken at death, remaining without perishing until resurrection, or withdrawn only from outward bodily life in sleep and sent back repeatedly until their appointed terms.
rows.anchor: في كيفية تعلق الأنفس بالأبدان وتوفيها عنها تارة بالكلية عند الموت وإمساكها باقية لا تفنى بفنائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who have exceeded bounds in sins have wronged themselves; some derive this figuratively in two steps from excess in spending, while al-Raghib defines excess as crossing bounds in any act, though spending is its common use, a definition Al-Alusi approves.
rows.anchor: على ما قيل وقال الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb includes the sense of committing injury, which permits its construction with على; an implicit sense need not be literal. Another analysis supplies the sense of bearing a burden.
rows.anchor: وضمن معنى الجناية ليصح تعديه بعلى والمضمن لا يلزم فيه أن يكون معناه حقيقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the possessive in My servants as covenantal or honorific and therefore understand the addressees as sinful believers, since the Quran commonly uses this divine possessive for believers.
rows.anchor: وحمل غير واحد الإضافة في ( عبادي ) على العهد أو على التشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command forbids despair of God's forgiveness and favor: forgiveness is either included in mercy or necessarily implied by it, since mercy cannot be conceived for someone unforgiven.
rows.anchor: أي لا تيأسوا من مغفرته سبحانه وتفضله عز وجل على أن المغفرة مدرجة في الرحمة أو أن الرحمة مستلزمة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reading treats the verse as an omitted-symmetry construction: do not despair of mercy and forgiveness, for God forgives all sins and shows mercy; Al-Alusi considers this strained.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون في الكلام صنعة الاحتباك كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness is explained either as overlooking sins and not punishing them inwardly or outwardly, which is their concealment, or as erasing them entirely from the records while overlooking them.
rows.anchor: المراد بمغفرة الذنوب التجافي عنها وعدم المؤاخذة بها في الظاهر والباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reads the unqualified promise as covering sins even without repentance, apart from associating partners, citing 4:48; he argues that restricting it to repentance is contrary to the verse's apparent wording.
rows.anchor: وأن الظاهر إطلاق الحكم وتقييده بالتوبة خلاف الظاهر كيف لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two indications for broad forgiveness are the address as servants, fitting a sinner's humility and inviting compassion, and the possessive relation to God, whose manner is to pity and care for His servant.
rows.anchor: الثاني الإختصاص الذي تشعر به الإضافة إلى ضميره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third indication is that the harm of excess falls on the sinners themselves, so their wrongdoing is already a sufficient injury; a wise person also finds the deserved punishment painful in itself.
rows.anchor: الثالث تخصيص ضرر الإسراف المشعرة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth indication for broad forgiveness is the unrestricted prohibition of despair from mercy, which extends even beyond a prohibition tied specifically to forgiveness.
rows.anchor: الرابع النهي عن القنوط مطلقا عن الرحمة فضلا عن المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth indication is mercy's attribution to the majestic name, encompassing all divine names; this signals breadth embracing repentant and unrepentant sinners.
rows.anchor: الخامس إضافة الرحمة إلى الاسم الجليل المحتوي على جميع معاني الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixth indication is the explanatory clause: not despairing of mercy without repentance is especially surprising, which suits a promise extending to the unrepentant.
rows.anchor: فإن التعليل يحسن مع الاستبعاد وترك القنوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventh indication is using God's majestic name instead of a pronoun, suggesting forgiveness follows from His very essence rather than requiring repentance or another cause.
rows.anchor: السابع وضع الاسم الجليل فيه موضع الضمير لإشعاره بأن المغفرة من مقتضيات ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eighth indication is the definite form of sins in a context of divine praise, which implies totality and thus includes sins followed by repentance and those not followed by it.
rows.anchor: الثامن تعريف الذنوب فإنه في مقام التمدح ظاهر في الاستغراق فتشمل الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ninth indication is the emphatic word all, reinforcing the promise's comprehensive scope.
rows.anchor: التاسع التأكيد بالجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tenth indication is the closing causal statement that God is forgiving and merciful, which supports the unrestricted promise.
rows.anchor: العاشر التعليل بأنه هو الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleventh indication is the intensive form ghafur: read quantitatively, it covers all sins; read qualitatively, it covers grave sins without repentance.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر التعبير بالغفور فإنه صيغة مبالغة وهي إن كانت باعتبار الكم شملت المغفرة جميع الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twelfth indication is that the object of ghafur is omitted, which conveys generality.
rows.anchor: فإن حذف المعمول يفيد العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thirteenth indication is exclusivity: since others can also be called forgiving, the exclusive predicate here means God's perfect, immense forgiveness, not forgiveness conditional on repentance.
rows.anchor: الثالث عشر إفادة الجملة الحصر فإن من المعلوم أن الغفران قد يوصف به غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourteenth indication is the further intensification of that exclusivity.
rows.anchor: الرابع عشر المبالغة في ذلك الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifteenth indication is that mercy is promised after forgiveness, implying the servant does not deserve forgiveness apart from God's mercy and supporting forgiveness without repentance.
rows.anchor: الخامس عشر الوعد بالحرمة بعد المغفرة فإنه مشعر بأن العبد غير مستحق للمغفرة لولا رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixteenth indication is the intensive form used for mercy.
rows.anchor: السادس عشر التعبير بعيغة المبالغة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventeenth indication is the unqualified expression of mercy.
rows.anchor: السابع عشر إطلاقها

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites deny that grave sins are forgiven without repentance; they qualify this verse by repentance verses, arguing that the case is one and the Quran functions as a single discourse, with no abrogation possible.
rows.anchor: ومنع المعتزلة مغفرة الكبائر والعفو عنها من غير توبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent addressees are the servants addressed earlier, whether that meant believers alone or believers together with unbelievers; what was sent down is the Quran, sent through Muhammad for all people.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه خطاب للعباد المخاطبين فيما تقدم سواء أريد بهم المؤمنون أو ما يعمهم والكافرين والمراد بما أنزل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible senses of the best are Quranic guidance to the good of both abodes, excluding stories and similar material; obligations; decisive obligations; or abrogating rulings. The comparative form is literal on the first and third readings, while the second and fourth allow two analyses.
rows.anchor: والمراد بأحسنه ما تضمن الإرشاد إلى خير الدارين دون القصص ونحوها أو المأمورية أو العزائم أو الناسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed sense is the safest and most secure course, such as turning back to God and persisting in obedience; the comparative then retains its ordinary force.
rows.anchor: لعل الأحسن ما هو أنجي وأسلم كالإنابة والمواظبة على الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A less apparent proposal makes the address one to jinn, takes what was sent down as the heavenly books, and identifies the best as the Quran; Al-Alusi notes the departure from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الخطاب للجني والمراد بما أنزل الكتب السماوية وبأحسنه القرآن وفيه ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Lord encourages obedience to what He sent down.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الرب ترغيب في الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is to follow before punishment arrives suddenly, with no awareness of its coming and no chance to take measures to avert it.
rows.anchor: لا تعلمون أصلا بمجيئه فتتداركون ما يدفعه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari construes the clause as a purpose object, supplying a deleted word meaning aversion and an omitted governing verb indicated by the preceding warning.
rows.anchor: في موضع المفعول له بتقدير مضاف وقدره الزمخشري كراهة وهو منصوب بفعل محذوف يدل عليه ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because he does not require subject identity for the governing verb, Al-Alusi allows anibū or ittabiʿū to govern the clause; construing the omitted noun as aversion is preferable to al-Hawfi's fear.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فهذه الكراهة مقابل الرضا دون الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The estimated aversion means the opposite of divine approval, not divine will, so this grammatical construction does not entail the Mu'tazilite doctrine of will.
rows.anchor: فهذه الكراهة مقابل الرضا دون الإرادة فلا اعتزال في تقديرها

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi instead estimates fear: the warning was given for fear that a soul might say this.
rows.anchor: كما فعل الحوفي حيث قال

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes anibū the governing verb and supplies neither aversion nor fear.
rows.anchor: وابن عطية جعل العامل ( أنيبوا )

rows.speaker: بعض النحاة
rows.claim: Some grammarians understand the construction as meaning lest a soul should say.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض النحاة إلى أن التقدير لئلا تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite soul may signal a multitude in context, as in al-A'sha's verse where one noble stands for crowds of supporters; alternatively it means some souls, which Abu Hayyan considers likelier and which suffices for a warning.
rows.anchor: وتنكير ( نفس ) للتكثير بقرينة المقام كما في قول الأعشى

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers the partitive sense, since only some souls need be the speakers for the threat to apply to every soul that might be one of them.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للتبعيض لأن القائل بعض الأنفس واستظهره أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed honorific sense is one uniquely distinguished soul, stubborn to an extreme or facing immense punishment; Al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون للتعظيم أي نفس متميزة من الأنفس إما بلجاج شديد أو بعذاب عظيم وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The alif replaces the possessive yā': Sibawayh explains the cry as calling regret to come, since its time has arrived.
rows.anchor: بالألف بدل ياء الإضافة والمعنى كما قال سيبويه يا حسرتي احضري فهذا وقتك

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the phrase in pause with hāʾ al-sakt, ya hasratah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير في الوقف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far has a possessive-yā' reading and another transmission combining compensatory alif with yā'; Al-Alusi calls the combination impermissible except as an exceptional usage and analogy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ( يا حسرتي )

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashf prefers treating the form as an emphatic dual, like labbayk and sa'dayk, following a dialect that retains dual alif in every case.
rows.anchor: فالأوجه أن يكون ثني الحسرة مبالغة على نحو لبيك وسعديك وأقام بين ظهريهم

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi allows a genuine dual in that dialect, referring to grief over missing paradise and entering the fire; Al-Alusi prefers the intensive reading because the sorrows of Judgment Day are many.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو الفضل الرازي في كتابه اللوامح أن تكون التثنية على ظاهرها على تلك اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means because of my neglect; على is causal, ما is a verbal noun, and tafrīt means falling short. The construction also occurs in 2:185.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب تفريطي فعلى تعليلية

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says janb literally names a bodily side and is borrowed for the side or direction adjoining it; here it figuratively means God's direction, with an omitted noun for obedience or His due, namely obedience.
rows.anchor: أصل الجنب الجارحة ثم يستعار للناحية والجهة التي تليها كعادتهم في استعارة سائر الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting the direction of obedience is a metonym for neglecting obedience itself; wasting the sphere entails wasting what it contains, making the inference especially forceful.
rows.anchor: والكلام على حذف مضاف أي في جنب طاعة الله أو في حقه تعالى أي ما يحق له سبحانه ويلزم وهو طاعته

rows.speaker: سابق البربري
rows.claim: Al-Alusi cites Sabiq al-Barbari's line about a lover's right as poetic evidence for janb meaning a direction or due.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك قول سابق البربري من شعراء الحماسة

rows.speaker: زياد الأعجم
rows.claim: Ziyad al-A'jam's verse about generosity, manliness, and liberality in a dome supplies an analogy for abstract qualities being assigned a place or direction.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك قول زياد الأعجم

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Imam explains janb as a side because necessary attendant matters resemble a limb or one of a thing's sides, allowing the word for a right, command, or obedience; he treats it as explicit metaphor without an omitted noun, a view Al-Alusi rejects.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام : سمي الجنب لأنه جانب من جوانب الشيء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as what the speaker neglected of God's reward.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن عباس : يريد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses it as what the speaker neglected of God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: ومقاتل : على ما ضيعت من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi understand it as neglecting God's command.
rows.anchor: ومجاهد والسدي : على ما فرطت في أمر الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as neglecting obedience to God.
rows.anchor: والحسن : في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr glosses it as neglecting God's due.
rows.anchor: وسعيد بن جبير : في حق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposal takes janb figuratively as God's essence, like side or assembly; Al-Alusi rejects it as awkward and unsuitable to apply to God even metaphorically.
rows.anchor: الجنب مجاز على الذات كالجانب أو المجلس يستعمل مجازا لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal makes janb a metaphor for proximity to God; Al-Alusi rejects it because it requires another metaphor and ultimately reduces to obedience or its like.
rows.anchor: هو مجاز على القرب أي على ما فرطت في قرب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase cannot be retained in its literal bodily sense, since God is transcendent above having a physical side.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة لا يمكن إبقاء الكلام على حقيقته لتنزهه عز وجل من الجنب بالمعنى الحقيقي

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Abdullah has fi dhikr Allah, in remembrance of God, in place of the phrase in the verse.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله زحفصة ( في ذكر الله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker says that he used to mock God's religion and its people.
rows.anchor: أي المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In is the lightened form of heavy inna, and the lām is the differentiating particle.
rows.anchor: و ( إن ) المخففة من الثقيلة واللام هي الفارقة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari takes the clause as circumstantial: the speaker neglected God's due while mocking.
rows.anchor: والجملة في محل النصب على الحال عند الزمخشري أي فرطت في حال سخريتي

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr considers it an independent statement about the speaker's former worldly state, intended to inform and intensify regret, not a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وقال في البحر : ويظهر أنها استئناف إخبار عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker claims that if God had guided him, he would have been among those guarded from idolatry and sins.
rows.anchor: أي من الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many interpret guidance as directing or showing the way that leads to faith, fitting the conditional and the reply beginning bala; Abu Hayyan instead interprets it as creating the act of guidance.
rows.anchor: وفسر غير واحد الهداية هنا بالإرشاد والدلالة الموصلة بناء على أنه الأنسب بالشرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi takes this statement as spoken in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وأيا كان فالظاهر أن هذه المقالة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karra means a return to worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي رجوعا إلى الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoped-for excellence would be in both creed and deeds.
rows.anchor: في العقيدة والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Law expresses a wish, and fa-akūna is subjunctive after the fa answering that wish.
rows.anchor: و ( لو ) للتمني ( فأكون ) منصوب في جوابها

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr also permits the subjunctive to coordinate with karra, which is a verbal noun, citing two poetic parallels; with fa as the wish's answer, an is obligatorily omitted and excellence follows the wished return, while coordination allows optional omission and makes excellence itself part of the wish.
rows.anchor: وجوز في البحر أن يكون منتصبا بالعطف على ( كرة )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and others interpret call upon Me as worship Me, and I will answer as I will reward you for it.
rows.anchor: أي اعبدوني أثبكم على ما روي عن ابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد وجماعة

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Asked to pray for someone, Sufyan al-Thawri said abandoning sins is prayer: spoken supplication expresses inward seeking and is valid only with genuine orientation and leaving disobedience; a sinner who persists is not truly asking even after a thousand invocations.
rows.anchor: الثوري أنه قيل له : ادع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says Sufyan's account supports interpreting supplication as worship, since abandoning sins is itself a major act of worship.
rows.anchor: وما ذكر مؤيد لتفسير الدعاء بالعبادة ومحقق له فإن ترك الذنوب من أجل العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daakhirin means subdued and abject.
rows.anchor: أي صاغرين أذلاء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi gives the alternative sense: ask Me, and I will give you what you ask for.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المعنى اسألوني أعطكم وهو المروي عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the asking interpretation, being arrogant toward worship means being arrogant toward supplication, which is worship and one of its best forms.
rows.anchor: يستكبرون عن دعائي لأن الدعاء من العبادة ومن أفضل أنواعها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said the best worship is supplication and recited this verse; al-Hakim authenticated the report, transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim.
rows.anchor: بل روي ابن المنذر والحاكم وصححه عن ابن عباس أنه قال : أفضل العبادة الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat addresses arrogance toward supplication, a habit of the affluent and extravagant; believers instead turn humbly to God through all their changing circumstances.
rows.anchor: والتوعد على الاستكبار عنه لأن ذلك عادة المترفين المسرفين وإنما المؤمن يتضرع إلى الله تعالى في كل تقلباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the object of arrogance to worship signals that supplication is a form of humility: worship entails submission, and asking God cannot itself be arrogance.
rows.anchor: وفي إيقاع العبادة صلة الاستكبار ما يؤذن بأن الدعاء باب من أبواب الخضوع لأن العبادة خضوع

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf finds the asking interpretation clearer and more contextual: the surah contrasts disputing God's signs in arrogance with supplicating and submitting to them in humility.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشف : وهذا الوجه أظهر بحسب اللفظ وأنسب إلى السياق

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf reads the conjunction as linking one complete narrative to another with the same purpose; the later passage at 40:69 makes explicit the surah's theme of refuting disputants, while its ending echoes the opening warning at 40:4.
rows.anchor: والعطف في قوله تعالى : ( وقال ) من عطف مجموع قصة على مجموع أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi agrees that the asking interpretation is clearer in wording: the worship interpretation requires two figurative moves, while the asking reading requires only one for My worship, or none if the possessive refers back to the prior mention; he is less convinced by the contextual argument.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره من أظهرية هذا الوجه بحسب اللفظ ظاهر جدا لما في الأولى من ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر قبل الحاجة إليه في موضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astajib is jussive as the answer to an imperative: if you call on Me, I answer you.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان ( فأستجب ) جزم في جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either interpretation, answering is conditional on God's will according to Al-Alusi's theological principles, as stated explicitly in 6:41.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة على الوجهين مشروطة بالمشيئة حسبما تقتضيه أصولنا وقد صرح بذلك في استجابة الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance toward worship, whether supplication or another form of worship, is unbelief and entails the threat stated in the verse.
rows.anchor: والاستكبار عن عبادة الله تعالى دعاء كانت أو غيره كفر يترتب عليه ما ذكر في الآية الكريمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refraining from supplication without arrogance can be blameworthy or appropriate, depending on the circumstance.
rows.anchor: وأما ترك ذلك لا عن استكبار فتفصيل الكلام فيه لا يخفى والمقامات في ترك الدعاء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says that whoever does not supplicate to God incurs His anger; Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shayba, and al-Hakim transmit it.
rows.anchor: من لم يدع الله تعالى يغضب عليه أخرجه أحمد وابن أبي شيبة والحاكم عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: As a counterexample of appropriate restraint, Abraham reportedly left supplication when thrown into the fire, saying that God's knowledge of his state made asking unnecessary; Al-Alusi presents this tentatively.
rows.anchor: وقد يحسن كما يدل عليه ما روي من ترك الخليل عليه السلام الدعاء يوم ألقي في النار وقوله علمه بحالي يغني عن سؤالي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Zayd b. Ali, and Abu Ja'far read the verb in the passive, meaning they will be admitted; transmissions differ from Asim and Abu Amr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر وزيد بن علي وأبو جعفر ( سيدخلون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is dry and drooping; khashi'a is borrowed from humility in the sense of submission.
rows.anchor: يابسة متعاطفة مستعار من الخشوع بمعنى التذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is rain.
rows.anchor: أي المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth moves with growth and swells: before a plant appears, the ground rises and expands, then splits to let the plant emerge.
rows.anchor: أي تحركت بالنبات وانتفخت لأن النبت إذا دنا أن يظهر ارتفعت له الأرض وانتفخت ثم تصدعت عن النبات

words: خَٰشِعَةً فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers a representative simile: the barren earth revived by rain resembles a gloomy, shabby person, ignored until worldly adornment makes him walk proudly; the comparison is omitted while its humbling and swaying features evoke it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في الكلام استعارة تمثيلية شبه حال جدوبة الأرض وخلوها عن النبات ثم إحياء الله تعالى إياها بالمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads raba'at with hamza, meaning increased; al-Zajjaj says raba means grew greatly, while the hamzated form means rose, as in rabī'a, a lookout on a high place.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : معنى ربت عظمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who revived the earth will revive the dead through resurrection.
rows.anchor: بما ذكر بعد موتها ( لمحي الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase every thing includes resurrection among the objects of divine power and intensifies the affirmation of that power.
rows.anchor: من الأشياء التي من جملتها الإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prescription reflects God's perfect knowledge and wisdom; tracing it to the named prophets shows an ancient religion agreed upon by the messengers.
rows.anchor: وإيذان بأنما شرع سبحانه لهم صادر عن كمال العلم والحكمة كما أن بيان نسبته إلى المذكورين عليهم الصلاة والسلام تنبيه على كونه دينا قديما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Muhammad's community and refers to the religion prescribed to Noah and later law-bearing messengers and resolute, renowned prophets, with a reinforced command.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لأمته عليه الصلاة والسلام أيشرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا ومن بعده من أرباب الشرائع وأولي العزم

words: نُوحًا وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These prophets are singled out for their rank and fame, and to draw unbelievers toward agreement: each group accepts a prophet, with Jews especially associated with Moses and Christians with Jesus.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص المذكورين بالذكر لما أشير إليه من علو شأنهم وعظم شهرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every prophet was commanded to establish Islam: affirm God's oneness and the enduring fundamentals of religious law and rulings that do not vary among peoples and ages.
rows.anchor: وإلا فما من نبي إلا وهو مأمور بما أمروا به من إقامة دين الإسلام وهو التوحيد وما لا يختلف باختلاف الأمم وتبدل الأعصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for enjoining signals the command's reinforcement and the care given to its subject.
rows.anchor: كما ينبيء عنه التوصية فإنها معربة عن تأكيد الأمر والاعتناء بشأن المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What was revealed to Muhammad may refer to the opening of this surah and 42:7, or more broadly to all revelations, including 16:123 and 18:110; Al-Alusi allows the broader reading.
rows.anchor: وإما ما يعمهما وغيرهما مما وقع في سائر المواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using revelation here, instead of the surrounding language of enjoining, matches the cited verses and explicitly asserts Muhammad's messengership against deniers; the honorific shift signals special care for him and his revelation.
rows.anchor: وإيثار الإيحاء على ما قبله وما بعده من التوصية لمراعاة ما وقع في الآيات المذكورة ولما في الإيحاء من التصريح برسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun alladhi marks Muhammad's revealed law as receiving the greatest care, explaining why it precedes the later named prophets despite coming later in time.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك إشعار بأن شريعته ص هي الشريعة المعتنى بها غاية الاعتناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is mentioned first to state promptly that the prescribed religion is ancient; Noah is also said to have been the first messenger.
rows.anchor: وتقديم توصية نوح عليه السلام للمسارعة إلى بيان كون المشروع لهم دينا قديما وقد قيل إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أول الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing the religion means maintaining Islam—God's oneness, obedience, belief in His books and messengers, the Day of Judgment, and all else that makes a servant a believer—and preserving its pillars from deviation while persevering in it.
rows.anchor: أي دين الإسلام الذي هو توحيد الله تعالى وطاعته والإيمان بكتبه ورسله وبيوم الجزاء وسائر ما يكون العبد به مؤمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An may be a verbal noun particle, or a lightened form of anna; the resulting verbal noun can be accusative as an appositive to the object of prescribed, or nominative as the predicate or subject of an elliptical clause answering the ambiguity about what was prescribed.
rows.anchor: و ( أن ) مصدرية وتقدم الكلام في وصلها بالأمر والنهي
